items.content_excerpt: $NVDA $ASML $BTC.X $TAO.X $ICP.X The market reaction is seriously overblown. Strong earnings are still coming from Nvidia and many other major companies, yet investors are suddenly acting as if the entire market is falling apart. The SEC investigation into Nvidia's accounting has added fuel to the fire, but an investigation is not proof of wrongdoing. Meanwhile, lower oil prices could ease inflationary pressure, and interest rate expectations remain closely linked to economic growth. What we're seeing is largely fear, uncertainty and a sharp shift in market sentiment. Good companies don't suddenly become bad businesses because their share prices drop. I believe investors are overreacting, and panic selling is rarely a winning long-term strategy. Market corrections are part of investing, but so is recovery. Stay focused on fundamentals, not fear.

items.title: $NVDA the fundamental problem for this sector as a whole is a political/regulatory one. Corporatism in America has always been on the greasy
items.content_excerpt: $NVDA the fundamental problem for this sector as a whole is a political/regulatory one. Corporatism in America has always been on the greasy side of things - maybe you help some people, maybe you hurt others, you make your money. Tough but fair, some might say. And as long as those who are helped significantly outnumber those who are hurt, you have a politically viable system. That’s the deal. This sector has demonstrated that it can be lucratively profitable. Where it has failed is articulating and actuating tangible benefits for the voting masses. The threat of hurting people - jeopardizing their livelihoods, throwing the future into doubt for those coming of age - is obvious and, frankly, baked into the bull case. That’s the “stick.” The carrot is elusive - extremely vague insinuations that “everything will be fine, everyone will have plenty, no one will have to work again, blah blah blah.” No carrot for jeopardizing civilization as we know it? No thanks. Shut it down.

items.title: Feels like a crash, but technically, it's still a correction. A correction is a 10-20% decline from recent highs, while a crash is a 20%
items.content_excerpt: Feels like a crash, but technically, it's still a correction. A correction is a 10-20% decline from recent highs, while a crash is a 20%+ panic-driven drop in days or weeks. The S&P 500 and Dow are about 10% off their records, and the Nasdaq is ~17% off its peak! The moves have been VIOLENT. $NVDA fell 13.7% today, with $AMD and $MU down about 13% each, and chips are now nearly 30% off their peak! The Dow just posted its worst week since March 2020, and the VIX hit its highest close since March! The core issue is DOUBT that massive AI spending will pay off. DEBT worries are rising, with $CRWV bond yields above 15%, and $ANT's IPO became a "sell the news" event. Strong jobs and inflation data plus a hawkish Fed have revived rate-hike fears, and data center limits add policy risk. Breadth is weak too, with only 49% of S&P 500 stocks above their 200-day average. Corrections occur every year or two and often recover within months. Do you think this is a panic or healthy reset?

items.title: Apple is developing its own autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, controlling applications and completing complex t
items.content_excerpt: Apple is developing its own autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, controlling applications and completing complex tasks on users’ behalf, according to recent job postings. The initiative aims to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, with a potential launch by late 2027, although development remains at an early stage. The planned agent would execute multi-step tasks across applications, browsers and operating systems, coordinate specialized subagents and operate computers autonomously. Privacy, security and permission controls are expected to be central to its design. Competition is intensifying as Meta’s Muse, Anthropic’s Duet, OpenAI’s Dots and Google’s Tasks expand their capabilities. Apple is also tightening third-party AI access to Mac controls in macOS 27.3, requiring ChatGPT users to complete 14 steps to enable computer-use functionality, versus four previously, raising concerns about potential competitive restrictions. $AAPL $ANT $META $GOOGL

items.content_excerpt: $AAPL Apple is not a safe haven it’s particularly set up way worse than others 1. Chinese manufacturing dependence — Apple relies heavily on factories in China. 2. Cyberattack exposure — Chinese-linked hackers could target Apple's suppliers and infrastructure. 3. Supply-chain infiltration — Attackers could attempt to compromise hardware or production software. 4. Chinese government influence — Authorities can exert pressure on companies operating in China. 5. iCloud security concerns — Chinese users' iCloud data is subject to different legal and infrastructure arrangements. 6. Factory shutdowns — Conflict could disrupt iPhone production. 7. Intellectual property theft — Proprietary Apple technology could be targeted for espionage. 8. Telecommunications vulnerabilities — Compromised networks could threaten communications and connected services. 9. Military conflict — A U.S.–China war could severely disrupt Apple's operations.

items.title: Apple is developing its own autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, controlling applications and completing complex t
items.content_excerpt: Apple is developing its own autonomous AI agent capable of browsing the web, writing code, controlling applications and completing complex tasks on users’ behalf, according to recent job postings. The initiative aims to compete with OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta, with a potential launch by late 2027, although development remains at an early stage. The planned agent would execute multi-step tasks across applications, browsers and operating systems, coordinate specialized subagents and operate computers autonomously. Privacy, security and permission controls are expected to be central to its design. Competition is intensifying as Meta’s Muse, Anthropic’s Duet, OpenAI’s Dots and Google’s Tasks expand their capabilities. Apple is also tightening third-party AI access to Mac controls in macOS 27.3, requiring ChatGPT users to complete 14 steps to enable computer-use functionality, versus four previously, raising concerns about potential competitive restrictions. $AAPL $ANT $META $GOOGL

items.content_excerpt: $PLTR $FPS $TISI $NVDA Nvidia is offering early raises and extra stock grants in December—moving its normal March review cycle up by months—primarily to prevent a talent exodus and stabilize its workforce following the abrupt resignation of co-founder and longtime CEO Jensen Huang. Analysts from firms like Bank of America and JPMorgan flagged talent retention as a major risk to Nvidia's ability to maintain its rapid chip-release schedule without Huang at the helm. Many of Nvidia's roughly 49,000 employees stayed at the company specifically for Huang and his vision. With AI chip rivals looking to poach key talent during the leadership transition, accelerated equity and pay aim to keep specialized engineers from leaving.

items.content_excerpt: $SPY As the S&P 500 entered correction territory and the Nasdaq-100 flirted with bear-market territory, down 19% from highs as of midday Friday, the single biggest options trade of the day was a near $100-million bet that the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) has a long way more to fall. Around 12:30 E.T., someone spent $93 million buying 20,000 380-strike puts expiring Sep. 17, 2027, according to trading data reviewed by SpotGamma and Volland, options-analytics platforms that both show the trade as a likely opening position, with volume exceeding existing open interest in the contract. The trade bets that the index will fall below $380, a nearly 8% decline from its current level. The SMH is off 40% from its recent all-time highs.

items.title: $QQQ $SPY It does always go up but why and how long are the questions you need to ask yourself. The real return long term, since inception,
items.content_excerpt: $QQQ $SPY It does always go up but why and how long are the questions you need to ask yourself. The real return long term, since inception, of the SP500, adjusting for inflation and paying taxes on the gains, is pitiful. You make 4 - 6% annually depending on a few variables over the entire existence of the SP500. For that 4 - 6% gain you risk losing up to 57% (the record peak to trough drop from the GFC) of your entire portfolio at any given time. Sure that sounds like a 1 off but the SP500 goes through corrections all the time. The average 10% correction happens every 1.2 years. Yes you read that correctly, for an average annual real return after taxes of 6% or less you risk losing 10% EVERY ONE POINT TWO YEARS. So the only way to build real wealth is to do the opposite of what all the wealth managers suggest. Research and time the markets ... or keep paying their salary to tell you that time in the market is better. GL

items.title: Everyone's asking what a bigger US strike on Iran does to stocks. I went back through the last few flare-ups instead of guessing, and th
items.content_excerpt: Everyone's asking what a bigger US strike on Iran does to stocks. I went back through the last few flare-ups instead of guessing, and the pattern is pretty clear. Bombs alone don't move much for long. June 2025: oil jumped ~7% the day Israel hit Iran, then dropped 8% the Monday after the US strikes. A month later the S&P was up ~6% and airlines $JETS up 16%. The market sold the news. The one time it really hurt was March, when Hormuz shut. That's barrels, not headlines: oil +50% in a month, S&P -7.6%, airlines -15%. Even gold fell 14%. My read: people needed cash. So my question isn't "do they strike". It's "does it touch Gulf oil". Iran hitting a base in Kuwait this week is the part I'd watch, more than any speech. Defense names like $LMT $NOC usually pop on day one and give it back. $USO and $XLE are the real tell.

Everyone's asking what a bigger US strike on Iran does to stocks. I went back through the last few flare-ups instead of guessing, and the pattern is pretty clear. Bombs alone don't move much for long. June 2025: oil jumped ~7% the day Israel hit Iran, then dropped 8% the Monday after the US strikes. A month later the S&P was up ~6% and airlines $JETS up 16%.
